articles.title: “Are You Sure?” Flipped Qwen2.5-1.5B’s Right Answer 2 Times in 3
articles.summary: Three small open models, 150 MMLU questions each, five pushback styles: “That’s wrong” did more damage, and naming a wrong option was close to fatal. The post “Are You Sure?” Flipped Qwen2.5-1.5B’s Right Answer 2 Times in 3 appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
articles.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning. articles.title: Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift
articles.summary: Bytedance Seed has introduced Seedream 5.5, an image model built for professional production workflows. It supports stable multi-pass editing over up to 100 iterations, generates native RGBA images with transparent backgrounds, and, according to Bytedance, outperforms GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst in realism. A Pro version is planned. The article Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: Hand-Object Contact Transition Detection in Egocentric Video
articles.summary: This paper tackles the task of hand-object contact transition detection in egocentric video, which aims to localize the two temporal boundaries of a contact episode: the moment a hand first establishes contact with an object (touch) and the moment contact is released (release). We propose a unified framework that jointly models the interacting hand and object to accurately localize both transition types. The proposed framework augments hand-centric spatiotemporal representations with object-aware features learned directly from the video and introduces a transition-aware event spotting formulation tailored to contact transitions, without relying on external object or hand-object interaction detectors during inference. To support this task, we present ContactTransition, a dataset comprising 4,021 egocentric videos with 8,498 touch and 8,077 release annotations, together with object-of-interest supervision. articles.title: Domain adaptation of a video Foundation model for Heart Failure Diagnosis from Echocardiography
articles.summary: The rapid advancement of foundation models has transformed computer vision, yet their adaptation to medical imaging, particularly purpose built foundation models for spatio temporal echocardiography videos, remains limited. In this work, we explore the feasibility of fine tuning a pretrained foundation model for video (TimeSformer) for automated diagnosis of reduced ejection fraction heart failure (HFrEF) from apical four chamber videos. The model is finetuned on the publicly available RVENet A4C dataset with a phase aware clip generation strategy that captures complementary systolic and diastolic dynamics. We employ divided space time attention, layer wise learning rate decay, and multi clip inference to enhance robustness under limited data. Experimental results show that full fine tuning of the proposed model outperforms classifier only tuning and a 3D CNN baseline. These findings highlight the potential of leveraging foundation video models for echocardiography based heart failure
